Hole features panel and PDF section: mock-up

DFMA Review · Inventor I2, slice S1 · 2026-11-09 · before any screen code

Proposal: a fold-away "Hole features" panel after Threads, plus a Hole features section on the PDF's first page after Threads. One row per Hole feature: its state (matched, disagrees or not mapped), its type and hole count, its sizes as designed in the .ipt (inches first, mm in brackets), and how many of its holes matched. Tapping a feature lights up all its holes in the 3D view and unfolds the holes that disagree or aren't mapped; tapping one of those shows that hole alone. The panel opens by itself when any hole disagrees or isn't mapped, and stays folded when every hole matched.

Your answer: Approve · Change (say what) · Rethink.

What the screenshots are

The real app, answered with the NIST CTC 04 pair lined up by the test harness (the app itself refuses NIST pairs, because NIST's STEP files come from another CAD system). The Findings list, 3D view and pins are real and already include the new "Hole feature vs hole" findings. Only the Hole features panel is drawn into the page for this mock-up, with the app's own styles.

Each disagreeing hole also has its finding page, like other findings.

Other states (proposed wording, not shown above)

  • No Hole features in the .ipt: the panel shows "No Hole features in this .ipt." and stays folded.
  • No .ipt: the panel is hidden; nothing changes for STEP-only users.
  • All matched: the panel is folded; its count still shows the number of features.

What doesn't change

The Threads panel, the Findings list layout, the 3D view and the Machine plan. The new findings sit in the Findings list under MEDIUM like the thread ones, labelled "Hole feature vs hole". Names like "Hole20" come in slice S2; until then a feature is shown by its id (hf-7).

Worth knowing before you approve

CTC 04 shows 13 disagreeing holes, not the 5 the spec expected. The spec counted only holes off their axis; the approved rule also compares diameter and depth, and NIST's two CTC 04 files differ there too. For example, hf-1's M12 holes: in the .ipt their Ø10.11 mm section is 25 mm long; in the STEP the hole is Ø10.20 mm and 30 mm long (the design depth 28.04 mm adds the drill point). These are measured differences between NIST's two files, which come from two CAD systems. Assumption: on a pair you export from Inventor yourself they would not appear; your work pair will show it (from 2026-11-12).

Two rules were settled while building, both measured on the NIST files: a hole and its mirror on one axis count as two holes (CTC 05 now has 21 holes, not 18), and a drill point cut short by a cavity doesn't close its hole (2 of 76 drill points, in CTC 04).
